description: We are developing TerraPulse, an AI-powered wildfire vulnerability and forest regeneration tracking platform using NASA FIRMS thermal anomaly data, Landsat 8/9 imagery, and NASA POWER climate data. Our goal is to empower emergency responders and conservationists with proactive early warnings and satellite-driven post-burn ecosystem monitoring. Passionate about Earth observation, AI, and open data for climate resilience.
summary:
A_A is an AI-driven environmental resilience platform designed to forecast wildfire risk and track post-fire forest regeneration using open satellite data. The system combines real-time thermal anomalies from NASA FIRMS (MODIS/VIIRS), meteorological metrics from the NASA POWER API, and multispectral surface reflectance from Landsat 8/9. 

Before a fire occurs, TerraPulse evaluates dry fuel biomass and climate parameters to pinpoint high-risk zones, giving emergency first responders 24 to 48 hours of proactive warning. Following a burn event, it computes spectral indices (NDVI and Normalized Burn Ratio) to evaluate damage severity and track natural vegetation regrowth over time. TerraPulse bridges the gap between raw space agency datasets and actionable ground-level conservation, safeguarding biodiversity, local communities, and forest ecosystems.
details:
What it does & How it works:

Our project, A_A (Team A_A), is an AI-powered environmental monitoring and predictive intelligence system that utilizes open satellite data from NASA to address wildfire threats and post-fire ecosystem recovery. The system operates in two core phases:

1. Pre-Fire Phase (Early Warning): Ingests real-time thermal anomaly observations from NASA FIRMS (MODIS/VIIRS) combined with atmospheric temperature, humidity, and rainfall data from the NASA POWER API. This calculates dry biomass risk and outputs a 1–5 Wildfire Susceptibility Score before ignitions peak.

2. Post-Fire Phase (Regeneration Tracking): Processes multispectral bands from Landsat 8 and 9 to compute the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) and Delta-NBR (dNBR), classifying burn scars into low, moderate, and high damage. It continuously tracks NDVI (vegetation density) curves over time to monitor forest regrowth.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Enables emergency responders and forestry departments to stage fire breaks and dispatch equipment 24–48 hours before extreme fire conditions occur.

- Supplies conservation agencies and NGOs with verified satellite data to guide reforestation and carbon sink restoration.

- Provides early alerts to vulnerable forest settlements and rural communities.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Languages & Libraries: Python, GeoPandas, Rasterio, NumPy, Scikit-learn

- Mapping & UI: Folium, Leaflet.js, Google Slides

- Satellite Data & APIs: NASA FIRMS API, NASA POWER API, USGS Landsat-8/9 Surface Reflectance

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Standard tools only track fires after they break out. TerraPulse is creative because it bridges proactive pre-fire hazard modeling with long-term post-fire ecosystem rehabilitation on a unified open-data platform. Our team prioritized computational accessibility, open-source tooling, and direct practical utility for ground-level rangers and disaster management teams.
